mode.description: How the subject is configured — for the horse family, `ride` (with a rider) or `lead` (with a handler on a rope). Distinct from `variant`, which is the coat, and from `tack`, which is what the horse wears in this configuration. Omit for an asset with only one configuration; a consumer uses its presence to tell a playable asset from a prop.

tack.description: What the subject is wearing in this configuration — for the horse family, `bareback`, `halter`, `saddled`, or `none` for a loose horse wearing nothing. A second axis beside `mode`: two assets may share a mode and differ only in tack, which is what lets a consumer offer a saddle toggle without parsing ids for a suffix. Omit it entirely for a family with no tack axis, which is not the same as `none`.

spritesheet.description: How spritesheet.png is laid out. Absent means the sheet is a single horizontal strip in `animations[0].order` sequence, which is the Slice 1/2 shape. A consumer that loads the packed sheet rather than the loose frames has no other way to map `order` onto pixels.

facing.description: Direction this clip faces. Omit for a non-directional asset — a prop has no facing, and requiring one would invalidate every static asset.

row.description: Row index of this clip in the packed sheet. Required when spritesheet.layout is row_per_animation.

next.description: The clip that follows when this one finishes, by `name`. Only meaningful with `loop: false`. Some gestures are authored as two rows that meet end to end rather than one looping row — the leading sheets draw petting as a lean-in and a lean-out whose endpoints match within 16 px — and a consumer has no other way to learn that playing one of them alone is half the gesture. A chain may be a cycle (a -> b -> a).

off_ground.description: Inclusive [first, last] frame indices where the subject has left the ground, measured from each frame's alpha bounding box against the clip baseline. Collision therefore tracks the artwork instead of a hand-tuned timer, and stays correct when fps changes.

sheet.description: Path of the sheet this clip was cut from, relative to the repository root.

row.description: Row of this clip in the SOURCE sheet, in that sheet's own grid.

columns.description: Source column of each frame of this clip, in order — `columns[i]` is where frame `i` came from. A list rather than a first-column-plus-count because a clip's frames are not always consecutive: `skip` in a pack leaves out a source frame the artwork gets wrong, and a contract that assumed consecutiveness would then point every frame after the gap at the wrong picture.

cell.description: The source sheet's own cell size, which is not the asset's: ingest re-blits every frame onto one common cell.

patched.description: Frames of this clip whose pixels do not match the source cell named above, because a declared correction in the pack restored something the artwork draws incompletely. Present so the difference reads as reviewed rather than as the pipeline corrupting the art; a viewer showing the source beside the output should say which frames it applies to. Corrections only ever copy pixels from elsewhere in the same sheet.

source.description: Where this clip came from. Provenance, not geometry — nothing needs it to draw. It exists so a defect can be reported against the artwork instead of against the packed output: a viewer showing 'frame 3 is wrong' can say which row and column of which sheet that frame actually is, which is the only form of that report a producer can act on. Omitted by producers with no single source row, such as the Path C stage graph.
